scope: CBSE Class 6 Social Science · Exploring Society: India and Beyond · Chapter 2 · Oceans and Continents
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 2 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action, and an observable mastery criterion.

scenarios.need: Learner overgeneralises the global land-water pattern and states that one hemisphere is entirely land or entirely ocean.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: hemisphere pattern turned into an absolute claim
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare two simplified offline hemisphere diagrams, identify land and water in both, and write a cautious comparison using words such as more, less and mostly.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Independently makes two accurate hemisphere comparisons without claiming that either hemisphere contains only land or only water.

scenarios.need: Learner treats a visual world map as an exact percentage measuring tool and memorises an unsupported land-water percentage instead of describing the broad pattern.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: visual area treated as exact numerical measurement
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a fictional equal-area comparison task to separate qualitative map evidence from exact numerical measurement and explain what conclusion the diagram actually supports.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly distinguishes broad geographic pattern evidence from exact measurement in two unfamiliar land-water examples.

scenarios.need: Learner omits one of the five named oceans or places an ocean on the wrong side of a continent.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: ocean names or relative locations incomplete
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use an offline blank world outline with movable labels for Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic, placing each relative to major continents.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly identifies and broadly locates all five named oceans on two unfamiliar simplified world maps.

scenarios.need: Learner treats named ocean boundaries as physical walls and assumes water or ships cannot pass between named oceans.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: named ocean boundaries treated as sealed barriers
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Trace fictional sea routes across named ocean regions on a public or offline world outline and explain why the labels change without a physical wall in the water.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains the interconnection of the global ocean in two new route examples while still naming the relevant ocean regions correctly.

scenarios.need: Learner confuses islands with continents or assumes size alone is enough to classify every land area.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Sort fictional and public land-region examples into continent, island or needs-more-context categories, using surrounding water and the working school convention rather than personal-location information.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly classifies unfamiliar island examples and distinguishes them from the seven working-continent labels with a clear reason.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes every source must use exactly seven continents and treats an alternative counting convention as automatically wrong.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: geographic convention mistaken for a single universal count
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare two fictional atlas legends, one using seven continents and one combining a land region, then identify the convention before comparing the counts.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses seven as the working school convention while accurately explaining in two examples why another source may use a different continent count.

scenarios.need: Learner lists ocean benefits or environmental problems without connecting cause, consequence and an appropriate prevention or shared-action response.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: ocean role and protection actions listed without causal reasoning
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use three fictional ocean-impact scenarios and complete a four-step chain: ocean role, human pressure, likely consequence, then prevention plus community or policy response.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains at least two ocean roles and designs balanced responses for two unfamiliar impact scenarios without unsupported advanced scientific claims.

scenarios.need: Learner needs a low-bandwidth, offline and instruction-light path that does not depend on video, live maps, GPS, microphone, camera, cloud AI or personal-data collection.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached text, a printed or locally drawn world outline and local assessment prompts; complete one Kiki step at a time without network-dependent tutoring or location disclosure.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes one ocean-protection reasoning task and its mastery check using local resources only, with no personal data, live location or remote service dependency.
